1. (The idea for this exercise is from Liza Bolton.) The following code makes a nice graph. Modify it to create the ugliest graph that you can.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Iris sepal dimensions",
    x = "Sepal length (cm)",
    y = "Sepal width (cm)",
    colour = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

2. Make a Quarto website and put it online. Create the project (`quarto create project website`), add a page with one graph of the shelter data from Week 1, set `output-dir: docs` in `_quarto.yml`, render, and push to a new GitHub repository. Under Settings, then Pages, deploy from `main` and the `/docs` folder. Write down the URL and open it on someone else's laptop.

3. Make three graphs from three different Open Data Toronto datasets using ggplot2, and one table using tinytable, and add them as a page on your website.
